corpusOverrides.note: 髦 left the flag list entirely: MM writes the two opening bars of 髟 in the opposite order (two strokes over 60°, max 94°) while the simplified file follows the dictionary with no stroke over 15°. 翻 dropped from six flagged strokes to four: the Japanese file also reorders the 番 body, and MM leaves only the four interior strokes of 羽, which then took authored paths. selection.json records both starting corpora and reasons.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: 髦 disappeared when the corpus changed. The rest were resolved by reordering (濛, 矇, 貓, 鮒) or by an authored path (廡, 翻). The endpoint assignment check added 紼, whose 糸 strokes run in the same direction and differ only in order; it also proposed a swap inside 麋 that the coordinates show to be a 10°/3° difference, so that one was left alone. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 9 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: All nine are short opening dots the dictionary draws vertically or steeper than the licensed corpora (炆 5 at 54°, 麋 1 at 55°, 糜 1 at 60°, 忞 1 at 59°, 亳 1 at 52°, 袢 1 at 52°, 辟 7 at 51°, 甓 7 at 53°, 掊 4 at 53°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: Three dictionary groups carry a horizontal offset, translate(12, -830), after 厲 in batch 4. serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y), and the published paths come from the licensed corpus, so the offset only affects what the review sheet draws.
